questions.question: A project manager drafting the procurement management plan has listed stakeholder roles, constraints and assumptions, contract types, decision criteria, prequalified sellers and a timeline. Which other items do the slides list as typical contents?

options.A: Each seller's detailed proposal, and its pricing
options.B: Metrics to manage contracts, and sponsor acceptance
options.C: The signed contracts, and the sellers' final invoices
options.D: Completed seller performance reviews, and audits

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Typical contents include stakeholder roles, constraints and assumptions, procurement requirements, contract types, decision criteria, prequalified sellers, a timeline, coordination with other project activities, metrics to manage contracts and sponsor acceptance. (LO2: Procurement Management Plan)
**Why not A:** Proposals arrive while conducting procurements, after the plan is written.
**Why not C:** Contracts and invoices come later; the plan describes how procurement will be managed.
**Why not D:** Performance reviews happen while controlling procurements.

questions.question: A sponsor asks where the project's procurement strategy is documented and what it defines. Which answer fits the slides?

options.A: In the procurement plan: delivery method, contract types, phases
options.B: In the SOW: deliverables, specifications and acceptance terms
options.C: In each contract: payment terms, penalties and closure steps
options.D: In the RFP: evaluation criteria, weighting and pricing rules

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** The procurement strategy is typically incorporated within the procurement management plan, and defines the project delivery method, the contract types and the procurement phases. (LO2: Procurement Strategy)
**Why not B:** The SOW describes the work required, not the overall procurement strategy.
**Why not C:** Contracts come after the strategy has shaped the procurement.
**Why not D:** The RFP solicits proposals; the strategy sits in the procurement management plan.

questions.question: After planning procurement, a project manager adds two new vendors to the preapproved seller list and revises the organization's procurement guidelines. Which kind of output is this?

options.A: Change requests raised for the project
options.B: A new statement of work for procurement
options.C: Updates to the project's documents
options.D: Updates to organizational process assets

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Other Plan Procurement outputs include change requests, project document updates and OPA updates, such as preapproved seller lists, procurement policies, procedures and guidelines, and contract types. (LO2: Other Plan Procurement Outputs)
**Why not A:** Change requests propose changes to the project; these are updates to organizational assets.
**Why not B:** A SOW describes the work to be procured, not seller lists or policies.
**Why not C:** Project document updates cover items like the lessons learned register, milestone list, requirements, and risk and stakeholder registers.

questions.question: To save time, a project manager copies last year's procurement management plan unchanged onto a very different project. What do the slides suggest?

options.A: Only the timeline needs updating for a new project
options.B: Plans are standard, so reusing one unchanged is expected
options.C: Contents vary with project needs, so it should be tailored
options.D: Sponsor acceptance makes later changes unnecessary

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** The procurement management plan's contents vary based on project needs; samples and templates are a starting point, not a copy-and-paste answer. (LO2: Procurement Management Plan)
**Why not A:** Requirements, contract types, criteria and sellers may all differ.
**Why not B:** The slides stress that contents depend on the project's needs.
**Why not D:** Sponsor acceptance is one item in the plan, not a reason to skip tailoring.

questions.question: Purchased equipment arrives at a construction site weeks before the foundations are ready, and must be stored at extra cost. Which part of the procurement management plan should have prevented this?

options.A: Listing the prequalified sellers for the equipment
options.B: Recording the sponsor's formal acceptance of the plan
options.C: Coordinating procurement with other project activities
options.D: Defining the metrics used to manage the contract

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Typical plan contents include a timeline of procurement activities and the coordination of procurement activities with other project activities. (LO2: Procurement Management Plan)
**Why not A:** Prequalified sellers help decide who to invite, not when deliveries should fit the work.
**Why not B:** Sponsor acceptance approves the plan; it doesn't coordinate deliveries with other work.
**Why not D:** Contract metrics track seller performance, not the fit between deliveries and site work.

questions.question: A buyer worries that a small firm bidding on a very large job might subcontract almost all of the work. Based on the slides' history of SOW problems, which clause addresses this?

options.A: Require a performance bond covering the full contract value
options.B: Require all of the work to be done at the buyer's own site
options.C: Require a firm fixed price that rules out any change orders
options.D: Name committed staff, with résumés and their time on the job

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** In the 1970s and 1980s small companies bid on mega jobs and subcontracted over 99% of the work; lawsuits followed, so SOWs began requiring the names and résumés of committed internal resources and their percentage of time. (LO2: Statement of Work)
**Why not A:** Bonds protect against non-performance, but the SOW fix described targets who will actually do the work.
**Why not B:** The slides' solution concerns identifying committed staff, not the work location.
**Why not C:** Pricing terms don't reveal whether the bidder will subcontract the work.

questions.question: A buyer's specification sets out the exact dimensions, materials and physical characteristics of a machined component. What type of specification is this, and who bears the risk of performance?

options.A: A performance specification, with the risk on the buyer
options.B: A functional specification, with the risk on the buyer
options.C: A design specification, with the risk on the contractor
options.D: A design specification, with the risk on the buyer

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** A design specification details what is to be done in terms of physical characteristics, and the risk of performance is on the buyer. (LO2: Statement of Work, Specifications)
**Why not A:** Performance specifications state measurable capabilities, and their risk sits with the contractor.
**Why not B:** Functional specifications describe end use, and their risk sits with the contractor.
**Why not C:** With a design specification, the buyer dictates the design, so the buyer carries the performance risk.

questions.question: A buyer states that a pump must deliver 500 litres per minute at a set pressure, and leaves the design entirely to the seller. What type of specification is this, and who bears the risk of performance?

options.A: A performance specification, with the risk on the contractor
options.B: A performance specification, with the risk on the buyer
options.C: A functional specification, with the risk on the buyer
options.D: A design specification, leaving the risk with the contractor

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** A performance specification states measurable capabilities the end product must achieve in operational terms, and the risk of performance is on the contractor. (LO2: Statement of Work, Specifications)
**Why not B:** Under a performance specification, the contractor carries the performance risk.
**Why not C:** Functional specifications describe the item's end use, and the risk is on the contractor.
**Why not D:** A design specification would dictate physical characteristics, and puts the risk on the buyer.

questions.question: To encourage competition among off-the-shelf products at a lower overall cost, a procurement document simply describes what the item will be used for. Which type of specification is this?

options.A: A design specification
options.B: A performance specification
options.C: A functional specification
options.D: A contract statement of work

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** A functional specification describes the end use of the item to stimulate competition among commercial items at a lower overall cost; the risk of performance is on the contractor. (LO2: Statement of Work, Specifications)
**Why not A:** A design specification details physical characteristics rather than end use.
**Why not B:** A performance specification sets measurable operating capabilities, not just the end use.
**Why not D:** A contract SOW describes the work under one contract; it isn't a type of specification.

questions.question: A hospital isn't sure what remote patient-monitoring products exist, and its requirements are still too vague to complete the SOW. Which bid document should it issue first?

options.A: A request for information (RFI)
options.B: A request for quotation (RFQ)
options.C: A request for bid (RFB)
options.D: A request for proposal (RFP)

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** An RFI is an informational tool used when requirements or the SOW are vague and the buyer wants to understand what exists in the marketplace; it's quick, can be informal, and can precede an RFQ or RFP. (LO2: Bid Documents, RFI)
**Why not B:** An RFQ needs detailed, precise requirements and strong market knowledge.
**Why not C:** A request for bid is another name for an RFQ, used for well-defined, price-based buys.
**Why not D:** An RFP is the final, complete solicitation document, which the hospital isn't ready to write.

questions.question: A vendor responding to a hospital's RFI asks whether its response commits either side to doing business together. What do the slides say?

options.A: No, although it does lock the buyer into a set price range
options.B: No: it flags a potential source but commits neither party
options.C: Yes: each responder must later submit a full proposal
options.D: Yes: the buyer must issue an RFQ to everyone who responds

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** An RFI signals the supplier as a potential source of supply but doesn't commit either party to future business; it's typically followed by an RFQ or RFP. (LO2: Bid Documents, RFI, RFQ and RFP)
**Why not A:** An RFI gathers information; it sets no prices.
**Why not C:** Responding to an RFI doesn't commit the vendor to anything further.
**Why not D:** An RFI may be followed by an RFQ or RFP, but it creates no obligation.

questions.question: A city knows the market and its qualified sellers well, and needs 500 laptops to a detailed, precise specification. The award will go to the best price that meets the delivery schedule. Which bid document fits?

options.A: A procurement management plan
options.B: A request for proposal (RFP)
options.C: A request for quotation (RFQ)
options.D: A request for information (RFI)

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** An RFQ is a price-comparison tool used when requirements and the SOW are detailed and precise and the buyer knows the market; it follows a formal, rigid competitive process focused on best price and schedule. (LO2: Bid Documents, RFQ)
**Why not A:** The plan describes how procurement is managed; it isn't sent to sellers.
**Why not B:** An RFP gives suppliers more latitude and suits requirements that are hard to describe.
**Why not D:** An RFI suits vague requirements and market exploration, not a precise buy.

questions.question: A retailer needs a new customer-experience platform, can't fully describe the requirement, and wants vendors to propose innovative approaches. Which bid document fits?

options.A: A request for information (RFI)
options.B: A request for proposal (RFP)
options.C: A request for quotation (RFQ)
options.D: A request for bid (RFB)

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** RFPs allow more latitude to the supplier than RFQs and are used when the requirement is difficult to describe or the purchaser expects innovation or creativity. (LO2: Bid Documents, RFP)
**Why not A:** An RFI gathers market information; it doesn't solicit full proposals.
**Why not C:** An RFQ asks for price and terms on a precisely defined requirement.
**Why not D:** A request for bid is used when a decision rests on price for a standard item.

questions.question: A procurement lead wants to save time by rushing out a short, rough RFP for a large, complex contract. What do the slides say about RFPs?

options.A: It's the final document, so it must be clear and complete
options.B: It's informal, so gaps can simply be fixed after award
options.C: It's only a quick precursor that comes before an RFI
options.D: It's mainly a tool for gathering market information

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** The RFP is the final document sent to prospective suppliers; it must be clear, complete and allow a competitive response, and preparing a good one for a large contract can be expensive and time-consuming. (LO2: Bid Documents, RFP)
**Why not B:** The slides describe the RFP as a critical document that must be complete.
**Why not C:** RFIs come before RFPs, not the other way round.
**Why not D:** Gathering market information is the RFI's purpose.

questions.question: A provincial agency is buying road salt, a standard item, and will choose the seller purely on price. What do the slides say such requests are often called?

options.A: A teaming agreement
options.B: A proposal for innovation
options.C: A request for information
options.D: A bid or tender

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** An RFQ (or request for bid) is a serious inquiry asking suppliers to declare price and terms; when the seller decision rests on price for a standard item, terms such as bid or tender are used. (LO2: Bid Documents, RFI, RFQ and RFP)
**Why not A:** Teaming agreements are strategic accords between companies on major projects.
**Why not B:** Proposals suit hard-to-describe needs where creativity is expected.
**Why not C:** An RFI explores the market without committing anyone to buy.

questions.question: A buyer is surprised that preparing its RFQ for 500 precisely specified laptops is taking weeks of work and a strict process. What do the slides say about RFQs?

options.A: They commit neither party to any future business
options.B: They take effort and follow a formal, rigid process
options.C: They give suppliers wide latitude to propose ideas
options.D: They're meant to be quick and informal, like an RFI

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** RFQs suit detailed, precise requirements and strong market knowledge; they may need significant time and effort to formulate and follow a formal, usually very rigid competitive process, which then simplifies evaluation. (LO2: Bid Documents, RFQ)
**Why not A:** That's a feature the slides give for RFIs, not a reason RFQs take effort.
**Why not C:** RFPs give suppliers more latitude than RFQs do.
**Why not D:** That describes RFIs, which can be developed quickly and informally.

questions.question: Before awarding a multi-year contract, a buyer reviews a seller's financial statements certified by an independent third party. Which source selection criterion is being applied?

options.A: Financial capacity and stability
options.B: Business capacity and interest
options.C: Customer reference checks
options.D: Seller capability and approach

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** A seller's ongoing ability is tied to its financial capacity and stability, which should be evaluated carefully, including a review of financial statements certified by an independent third party. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not B:** That criterion concerns capacity to deliver (for example, via site tours) and the seller's interest in the buyer's business.
**Why not C:** References come from the seller's past clients, not from audited statements.
**Why not D:** That criterion asks whether the seller has the required capability to deliver under contract.

questions.question: A buyer tours a seller's facilities to confirm it can handle the required volume, and gauges how interested the seller is in the buyer's business. Which source selection criterion is this?

options.A: Acceptance and warranty
options.B: Financial capacity and stability
options.C: Management approach
options.D: Business capacity and interest

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Business capacity and interest asks whether the seller has adequate capacity to deliver under the agreement (which may require site tours) and how interested it is in the buyer's business. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not A:** That criterion concerns standing behind products and remedying deficiencies.
**Why not B:** That criterion focuses on financial resources and certified financial statements.
**Why not C:** That criterion concerns culture fit and how the seller manages delivery.

questions.question: For a construction project overseas, a buyer checks whether each bidder can source local workers and resources in that country. Which source selection criterion is this?

options.A: Management approach
options.B: Business capacity and interest
options.C: Capability and approach
options.D: Diversity sellers

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Capability and approach asks whether the seller has the required capability; in international procurement, specific capabilities such as sourcing local workers or resources must be evaluated. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not A:** That criterion concerns culture fit and the approach to managing delivery.
**Why not B:** That criterion concerns the volume a seller can handle and its interest in the buyer's business.
**Why not D:** That criterion concerns awarding a share of work to minority-, woman- or veteran-owned firms.

questions.question: One bidder offers a defined acceptance period with remedies, commits to correct any non-conforming items or refund the money, and backs its work with a long warranty. Which criterion does this strengthen, according to the slides?

options.A: Pricing
options.B: Intellectual property and proprietary rights
options.C: Contract commitments and risk
options.D: Acceptance and warranty

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** The slides treat a seller's willingness to stand behind its work, with an acceptance period, remedies and a warranty period and coverage, as a strong indication of its ability to deliver or perform. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not A:** Pricing is a separate criterion; this offer is about standing behind the work.
**Why not B:** That criterion concerns ownership and rights to the work, not remedies for defects.
**Why not C:** That criterion is listed separately and doesn't centre on acceptance periods and warranties.

questions.question: A public agency must award a set percentage of its procurements to minority-owned, woman-owned or veteran-owned firms. Which source selection criterion is this, and why do organizations use it?

options.A: Management approach, to make sure the cultures fit
options.B: Customer reference, to confirm past clients were satisfied
options.C: Diversity sellers, partly to look favourable to the public
options.D: Business capacity, to confirm the firms can handle volume

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Some organizations require that a certain percentage of procurements go to diversity sellers such as minority-, woman- or veteran-owned firms, in part to be viewed in a favourable light by the public. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not A:** Culture fit is a different criterion from diversity requirements.
**Why not B:** References check a seller's track record, not its ownership.
**Why not D:** Capacity concerns ability to deliver, not the ownership of the seller.

questions.question: A buyer phones a seller's past clients to ask how satisfied they were with its performance and staff, whether it understood their needs and communicated clearly, and whether the value matched the price. Which criterion is this?

options.A: Seller understanding of project needs
options.B: Business capacity and interest
options.C: Customer reference
options.D: Financial capacity and stability

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Customer reference checks ask past clients about performance, delivery, staff skills, understanding of needs, communication, and whether value matched price; the process can provide significant value. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not A:** That criterion assesses the seller's grasp of this project, typically from its response.
**Why not B:** That criterion concerns capacity to deliver and interest in the buyer's business.
**Why not D:** That criterion reviews certified financial statements, not client feedback.

questions.question: One bidder's proposal restates the buyer's requirements in generic terms and never addresses the operational problem the project is meant to solve. On which source selection criterion will it score poorly?

options.A: Diversity seller requirements
options.B: Seller understanding of project needs
options.C: Acceptance and warranty terms
options.D: Seller financial capacity and stability

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** The slides list the seller's understanding of the project's needs among the things a buyer should consider when developing source selection criteria. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not A:** That criterion concerns minority-, woman- or veteran-owned sellers.
**Why not C:** That criterion concerns standing behind the delivered work.
**Why not D:** That criterion reviews financial strength, not the seller's grasp of the project.

questions.question: A software vendor's proposal states that the vendor will keep ownership of any custom code it writes for the buyer. Which listed source selection criterion should the committee weigh here?

options.A: Intellectual property and proprietary rights
options.B: Seller management approach and culture fit
options.C: Customer references from the seller's past clients
options.D: Business capacity and interest in the work

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** The slides list intellectual property and proprietary rights among the source selection criteria, alongside contract commitments and risk, and pricing. (LO2: Source Selection Criteria)
**Why not B:** That criterion concerns how the seller manages delivery and fits the buyer's culture.
**Why not C:** References concern past clients' satisfaction, not who owns the code.
**Why not D:** That criterion concerns the seller's capacity to deliver and its interest in the buyer's business.

questions.question: During a competitive procurement, a seller phones a committee member directly to ask how its proposal is being scored. What should the committee member do?

options.A: Pass the call to another committee member to handle
options.B: Send the seller back to the buyer, per the protocol
options.C: Answer informally to keep the relationship friendly
options.D: Share the scoring criteria to keep the process open

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Committee members should re-direct sellers that don't follow the communication protocol to the buyer and keep the committee's work confidential. (LO2: Seller Selection Committee, Roles and Cautions)
**Why not A:** Sellers who bypass the protocol should be sent to the buyer, not to other members.
**Why not C:** Informal answers break the communication protocol and the committee's confidentiality.
**Why not D:** The committee's work must be kept confidential.

questions.question: Partway through evaluations, a committee member realizes their spouse works for one of the bidders. What do the slides say the member must do?

options.A: Recuse themself from the committee immediately
options.B: Disclose it, but keep scoring that bidder fairly
options.C: Score that bidder lower to show neutrality
options.D: Stay on, and recuse only if that bidder wins

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** Committee members must immediately recuse themselves in the case of an actual or apparent conflict of interest. (LO2: Seller Selection Committee, Cautions)
**Why not B:** Even an apparent conflict requires immediate recusal.
**Why not C:** Adjusting scores is unfair; the member must step aside.
**Why not D:** Recusal must be immediate, not after the outcome.

questions.question: At a bidder conference, several sellers ask committee members for their business cards so they can follow up. How do the slides say members should handle this?

options.A: Assign one member as each seller's main contact
options.B: Publish the full committee list to show fairness
options.C: Exchange contacts to make follow-up questions easier
options.D: Be introduced, but give out no contact details

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** At seller conferences, committee members may be introduced to sellers, but no contact information should be disclosed; no one outside the committee needs to know its composition or members' information. (LO2: Seller Selection Committee, Cautions)
**Why not A:** Sellers communicate through the buyer, not through committee members.
**Why not B:** The committee's composition should stay confidential.
**Why not C:** Contact information must not be disclosed to sellers.

questions.question: After shortlisting sellers, a committee is planning its remaining work. Which tasks do the slides list as committee duties at this stage?

options.A: Sign the final contract on the organization's behalf
options.B: Inspect delivered goods and approve the seller's payments
options.C: Approve the project budget and the project charter
options.D: Plan a best and final offer, and debrief losing sellers

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Duties include short-listing sellers, helping develop negotiation strategies such as best and final offer, conducting due diligence, and participating in debriefing unsuccessful sellers. (LO2: Seller Selection Committee, Role and Duties)
**Why not A:** Signing isn't listed among the committee's duties.
**Why not B:** Inspection and payment happen after award, under contract administration.
**Why not C:** Budget and charter approval aren't committee duties.

questions.question: Short on time, a committee member reads only the two proposals they already favour and skips scoring the rest. Which committee duty is being neglected?

options.A: Reading every response and scoring it on the matrix
options.B: Debriefing the sellers who were not successful
options.C: Helping draft answers to sellers' written questions
options.D: Attending the pre-proposal bidder conference in person

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** Committee members must read all responses received and make notations in or on the proposal evaluation matrix, and help develop the evaluation criteria and weighting. (LO2: Seller Selection Committee, Role and Duties)
**Why not B:** Debriefing happens after award, not during evaluation.
**Why not C:** That duty happens during the solicitation, not during scoring.
**Why not D:** Attending the conference is a separate duty, before proposals arrive.

questions.question: During due diligence, a committee member uncovers weak references for a leading bidder, but stays quiet at the scoring meeting to avoid conflict. What do the slides expect of committee members?

options.A: Lower that bidder's score without explaining why
options.B: Discuss their findings and scores openly and objectively
options.C: Keep findings private to protect the seller's reputation
options.D: Report the findings directly to the bidder concerned

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Committee duties include conducting due diligence on sellers and openly and objectively discussing individual findings and scoring at the meeting. (LO2: Seller Selection Committee, Role and Duties)
**Why not A:** Unexplained scoring changes aren't objective; findings should be discussed openly.
**Why not C:** Confidentiality applies outside the committee; within it, findings should be discussed openly.
**Why not D:** Communication with sellers goes through the buyer, not through committee members.

questions.question: An organization wants to know whether its procurement function is sophisticated enough to use the procurement knowledge area as a structured methodology, and where its gaps in organizational process assets lie. Which tool fits?

options.A: A make-or-buy decision analysis
options.B: The Procurement Maturity Model
options.C: A request for information (RFI)
options.D: A pre-proposal bidder conference

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** The Procurement Maturity Model gauges the performance and maturity level of a procurement function and helps define where there are gaps in OPAs. (LO2: Procurement Maturity)
**Why not A:** Make-or-buy analysis decides whether to make or purchase specific items.
**Why not C:** An RFI gathers information from the market about products and services.
**Why not D:** Bidder conferences clarify bid documents for sellers.

questions.question: At one company, procurement is an afterthought buried deep in the hierarchy, customers and suppliers avoid interacting with it, and its employees are actively disengaged. Where does it sit in the Procurement Maturity Model?

options.A: At the top levels: best in class or world class
options.B: At the optimizing level, just below best in class
options.C: At the lowest levels: inhibiting or performing
options.D: At the middle levels: enabling or optimizing

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** In the model, the bottom levels (performing and inhibiting) feature procurement as an afterthought, not a core competency, with customers and suppliers avoiding interaction and employees actively disengaged. (LO2: Procurement Maturity Model, Levels of Maturity)
**Why not A:** The top levels treat procurement as a strategic core competency reporting to the C-level.
**Why not B:** Optimizing organizations see procurement as value-add, unlike this company.
**Why not D:** The middle levels see procurement as value-add, with some executive support and engaged employees.

questions.question: At another company, procurement is seen as a 'value-add' function with some executive support and investment, customers and suppliers are mostly satisfied, and there's some pursuit of best practices. Where does it sit in the model?

options.A: At the top levels: best in class or world class
options.B: At the world class level only
options.C: At the lowest levels: inhibiting or performing
options.D: At the middle levels: enabling or optimizing

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** The middle levels (enabling and optimizing) see procurement as value-add, with some executive support and investment, mostly satisfied customers and suppliers, engaged employees and some pursuit of best practices. (LO2: Procurement Maturity Model, Levels of Maturity)
**Why not A:** The top levels add a strategic core competency, certified staff, high automation and metrics.
**Why not B:** World class goes well beyond value-add, to procurement as a strategic core competency.
**Why not C:** The lowest levels treat procurement as an afterthought with disengaged employees.

questions.question: A third company treats procurement as a strategic core competency reporting to the C-level, staffs it with degreed and certified professionals, automates heavily, manages by metrics and supports supplier diversity and development. Where does it sit?

options.A: At the top levels: best in class or world class
options.B: At the performing level, above inhibiting
options.C: At the middle levels: enabling or optimizing
options.D: At the lowest levels: inhibiting or performing

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** The top levels describe procurement as strategic and a core competency reporting to the C-level, staffed with qualified professionals, highly automated, metrics-driven, and looking beyond itself. (LO2: Procurement Maturity Model, Levels of Maturity)
**Why not B:** Performing is one of the lowest levels, far from this profile.
**Why not C:** Middle levels see procurement as value-add with only some executive support.
**Why not D:** Lowest levels treat procurement as an afterthought.
